{"findings": [
  {
    "file": "app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb",
    "line": 66,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Automatic downsize ignores conversion failure and final size",
    "body": "The loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize and decrements attempt, but ignores the boolean returned by downsize and never checks after the loop whether tempfile.size is still greater than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. If ImageMagick/gifsicle fails (corrupt image, mislabeled non-image, unsupported format) or five 80% reductions are insufficient, create_upload proceeds with the same tempfile. This can reject the upload only later with a generic error, or store an oversized/corrupt image depending on the rest of the model validation. The code should break on successful downsize and return an explicit error if the final file is still over the limit."
  },
  {
    "file": "app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb",
    "line": 55,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "URL download limit is hardcoded to 10 MB and ignores site settings",
    "body": "FileHelper.download now uses 10.megabytes instead of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. Non-image URL uploads do not go through the later image downsize loop, so this action can fetch up to 10 MB even if the configured max_image_size_kb is much lower. Conversely, sites with max_image_size_kb above 10 MB can no longer fetch such files via URL. Use the configured limit for non-image uploads or enforce it explicitly after download."
  },
  {
    "file": "app/assets/javascripts/discourse/lib/utilities.js",
    "line": 182,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "bug",
    "title": "Client upload validation hardcodes 10 MB instead of per-type site settings",
    "body": "validateUploadedFile no longer reads Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so both image and attachment client-side checks now use 10 MB. The 413 handler at line 246 does the same instead of using max_image_size_kb. Sites with a smaller configured limit still allow the browser to submit oversized files, while sites with a larger configured limit have valid uploads blocked by the client. The alert text can also report the wrong maximum size. Keep using the site settings or add a separate consistent cap."
  },
  {
    "file": "app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb",
    "line": 67,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "data",
    "title": "Animated GIFs are flattened because downsize sees the tempfile path, not the original filename",
    "body": "OptimizedImage.downsize decides whether to use the animated downsize path by testing the source path for a .GIF extension in OptimizedImage.optimize. Here the source path is tempfile.path, which for Rack uploads is typically a generated /tmp/RackMultipart... path without the original .gif extension, while the original filename is available separately. As a result, oversized animated GIF uploads are processed by the normal ImageMagick instructions with from[0], which reads only the first frame and throws away the animation. The original filename/extension must be preserved on the tempfile or passed into the downsize call so the animated branch can be selected."
  },
  {
    "file": "app/models/optimized_image.rb",
    "line": 149,
    "severity": "high",
    "category": "api",
    "title": "Redefining self.downsize overrides the existing four-argument method",
    "body": "Ruby does not support overloading, so the new def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) replaces the previous def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}). Any caller using OptimizedImage.downsize(path, out, width, height) now binds width as dimensions and height as opts. The next downsize call may then evaluate opts[:allow_animation] on an Integer and raise TypeError, or silently ignore the height. Remove one of the duplicate methods and provide a single supported signature."
  },
  {
    "file": "app/models/optimized_image.rb",
    "line": 153,
    "severity": "medium",
    "category": "api",
    "title": "OptimizedImage.optimize signature change breaks positional width/height callers",
    "body": "optimize changed from optimize(operation, from, to, width, height, opts={}) to optimize(operation, from, to, dimensions, opts={}). Direct callers that still pass width and height as two arguments will now have height treated as opts, causing TypeError when opts[:allow_animation] is evaluated or otherwise incorrect behavior. If this is meant as an internal API, make that explicit and update all consumers; otherwise keep a backwards-compatible shim."
  },
  {
    "file": "app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb",
    "line": 63,
    "severity": "low",
    "category": "test_gap",
    "title": "No tests added for auto-downsize behavior",
    "body": "The PR adds server-side downsize-on-upload, changes OptimizedImage method signatures, and changes client validation, but no specs are included. Boundaries around max_image_size_kb, downsize failure, insufficient reduction, animated GIFs, and non-image uploads are untested. A test for the previous OptimizedImage.downsize call style would also have caught the duplicate method issue."
  }
]}

findings.title: Automatic downsize ignores conversion failure and final size
findings.body: The loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize and decrements attempt, but ignores the boolean returned by downsize and never checks after the loop whether tempfile.size is still greater than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. If ImageMagick/gifsicle fails (corrupt image, mislabeled non-image, unsupported format) or five 80% reductions are insufficient, create_upload proceeds with the same tempfile. This can reject the upload only later with a generic error, or store an oversized/corrupt image depending on the rest of the model validation. The code should break on successful downsize and return an explicit error if the final file is still over the limit.

findings.title: URL download limit is hardcoded to 10 MB and ignores site settings
findings.body: FileHelper.download now uses 10.megabytes instead of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. Non-image URL uploads do not go through the later image downsize loop, so this action can fetch up to 10 MB even if the configured max_image_size_kb is much lower. Conversely, sites with max_image_size_kb above 10 MB can no longer fetch such files via URL. Use the configured limit for non-image uploads or enforce it explicitly after download.

findings.title: Client upload validation hardcodes 10 MB instead of per-type site settings
findings.body: validateUploadedFile no longer reads Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so both image and attachment client-side checks now use 10 MB. The 413 handler at line 246 does the same instead of using max_image_size_kb. Sites with a smaller configured limit still allow the browser to submit oversized files, while sites with a larger configured limit have valid uploads blocked by the client. The alert text can also report the wrong maximum size. Keep using the site settings or add a separate consistent cap.

findings.title: Animated GIFs are flattened because downsize sees the tempfile path, not the original filename
findings.body: OptimizedImage.downsize decides whether to use the animated downsize path by testing the source path for a .GIF extension in OptimizedImage.optimize. Here the source path is tempfile.path, which for Rack uploads is typically a generated /tmp/RackMultipart... path without the original .gif extension, while the original filename is available separately. As a result, oversized animated GIF uploads are processed by the normal ImageMagick instructions with from[0], which reads only the first frame and throws away the animation. The original filename/extension must be preserved on the tempfile or passed into the downsize call so the animated branch can be selected.

findings.title: Redefining self.downsize overrides the existing four-argument method
findings.body: Ruby does not support overloading, so the new def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) replaces the previous def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}). Any caller using OptimizedImage.downsize(path, out, width, height) now binds width as dimensions and height as opts. The next downsize call may then evaluate opts[:allow_animation] on an Integer and raise TypeError, or silently ignore the height. Remove one of the duplicate methods and provide a single supported signature.

findings.title: OptimizedImage.optimize signature change breaks positional width/height callers
findings.body: optimize changed from optimize(operation, from, to, width, height, opts={}) to optimize(operation, from, to, dimensions, opts={}). Direct callers that still pass width and height as two arguments will now have height treated as opts, causing TypeError when opts[:allow_animation] is evaluated or otherwise incorrect behavior. If this is meant as an internal API, make that explicit and update all consumers; otherwise keep a backwards-compatible shim.

findings.title: No tests added for auto-downsize behavior
findings.body: The PR adds server-side downsize-on-upload, changes OptimizedImage method signatures, and changes client validation, but no specs are included. Boundaries around max_image_size_kb, downsize failure, insufficient reduction, animated GIFs, and non-image uploads are untested. A test for the previous OptimizedImage.downsize call style would also have caught the duplicate method issue.
